elements.name: Arbitrary-Precision Arithmetic
elements.what: Represent and compute on integers (or rationals/decimals) whose size is limited only by memory, using multi-limb representations and carry-propagating algorithms instead of fixed-width machine words.
elements.problem: Fixed-width machine integers overflow; cryptography, computer algebra, financial and exact computation need results beyond 64 bits with exact semantics.
elements.named_in: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming Vol. 2: Seminumerical Algorithms, sec. 4.3 'Multiple-Precision Arithmetic'

elements.name: Pseudorandom Number Generator
aka: LCG / Mersenne Twister / xorshift / PCG (algorithm variants, folded)
elements.what: A deterministic state machine that expands a seed into a stream of statistically random-looking numbers, giving reproducible randomness on demand.
elements.problem: Programs need randomness (simulation, games, sampling, testing) that is fast, portable, and — via the seed — exactly reproducible for replay and debugging; true entropy sources provide none of these.
elements.named_in: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming Vol. 2: Seminumerical Algorithms, ch. 3 'Random Numbers'
tags: borderline: algorithm-flavored; included as the deterministic, seeded-reproducibility counterpart of the already-cataloged csprng, with algorithm variants folded into aka

elements.name: LR Parser
elements.what: Bottom-up table-driven parsing: a state stack plus action/goto tables shifts input tokens and reduces recognized handles to grammar nonterminals.
elements.problem: Recursive descent cannot directly handle left recursion or many deterministic context-free grammars; generating a shift-reduce table mechanically from the grammar gives linear-time parsing with grammar-level maintainability.
elements.named_in: Aho, Sethi, Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools (the Dragon Book), ch. 4
tags: canonical counterpart of recursive-descent-parser already in catalog

elements.name: Logical Clock
elements.what: A per-process counter (scalar or vector) advanced on local events and merged on message receipt so that timestamp order respects causal (happened-before) order without synchronized physical clocks.
elements.problem: Concurrent and distributed components need to order events, detect causality, and version state when wall clocks are unreliable or unavailable.
elements.named_in: Lamport, 'Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System', CACM 1978
tags: in-process mechanism precedent: crdt and operational-transformation already in catalog

elements.name: Parallel Reduction
elements.what: Combine a collection of values into one result with an associative operator arranged as a tree of partial reductions computed in parallel, then merged.
elements.problem: A sequential fold serializes aggregation; exploiting associativity turns O(n) dependent steps into parallel partials plus O(log n) merge, without data races on a shared accumulator.
elements.named_in: McCool, Robison, Reinders, Structured Parallel Programming: Patterns for Efficient Computation (2012)
tags: peer of loop-parallelism / fork-join / pipeline-parallelism already in catalog

elements.name: Stencil
elements.what: Update every element of a regular grid as a fixed function of its spatial neighborhood, typically double-buffered between generations and tiled/parallelized over the grid.
elements.problem: Grid computations (image filters, cellular automata, PDE solvers, convolution) share a regular neighbor-access shape whose naive form thrashes caches and races on in-place updates.
elements.named_in: McCool, Robison, Reinders, Structured Parallel Programming: Patterns for Efficient Computation (2012), stencil chapter
tags: borderline: domain-parallel kernel shape at the algorithm-zoo edge; kept on pattern-catalog naming and cross-domain recurrence

elements.name: Content-Addressable Storage
elements.what: Store immutable blocks/objects keyed by a cryptographic hash of their contents, so identical data coalesces, references are self-verifying, and writes are idempotent.
elements.problem: Location-addressed storage cannot cheaply deduplicate, verify integrity, or share immutable history; hashing the content makes the identifier both the address and the checksum.
elements.named_in: Quinlan & Dorward, 'Venti: A New Approach to Archival Storage', USENIX FAST 2002 (verified live); canonical modern realization: the Git object store

elements.name: Privilege Separation
elements.what: Split one application into a small privileged process and unprivileged worker processes that request sensitive operations over a narrow IPC interface, so a compromise of the exposed code yields no privileges.
elements.problem: Monolithic privileged programs let any exploited parsing/network-facing code inherit full privileges; confining privileges to a minimal monitor bounds the damage.
elements.named_in: Provos, Friedl, Honeyman, 'Preventing Privilege Escalation', 12th USENIX Security Symposium 2003 (verified live)
tags: borderline: multi-process internal structure edges toward architecture; kept design-realm because it is a named mechanism implemented within one application (privilege-bracketing covers only the temporal form)

elements.name: Four-Phase Test
elements.what: Structure every test as four ordered phases — fixture setup, exercise the system under test, result verification, fixture teardown — one behavior per test.
elements.problem: Unstructured test methods interleave setup, actions and assertions, hiding what is tested and leaking state between tests; a fixed phase skeleton makes intent and independence mechanical.
elements.named_in: Meszaros, xUnit Test Patterns (2007); xunitpatterns.com 'Four Phase Test' (verified live)
tags: borderline: test-code structuring pattern near the practice boundary; included on Meszaros catalog establishedness and the composed-method altitude precedent

notes: FINAL ADVERSARIAL VERDICT: SATURATED — stop per mission rule 4. Evidence: (1) This mandated closer hunt, run with fresh eyes over all 682 entries plus targeted probes of every thin axis and unswept domain, yielded 9 additions of which only 5 are non-borderline (arbitrary-precision-arithmetic, lr-parser, logical-clock, parallel-reduction, content-addressable-storage) — at the ~5 threshold, and 3 of those 5 sit exactly in the axes pre-identified as thin (numeric-precision, parsing-text), i.e. the finds are residue of known thinness, not evidence of an unswept seam. (2) The rejection record (30 checked-and-rejected candidates + 6 parks) shows the remaining candidate space collapses into four closed classes: folds into existing aka, algorithm zoo, practice/tooling, and upward-architecture parks. (3) Source cross-check: GoF 23/23 present; POSA1/POSA2 pattern lists fully present; Nystrom complete; EIP mid-level subset, Fowler PoEAA, Hanmer, Beck SBPP, Douglass, JCiP all swept; the only canonical catalog with a residual title-level gap was Meszaros xUnit Test Patterns (four-phase-test, now added). (4) Calibration-anchor audit: all mission anchors resolve to catalog entries (semantic-data-types is carried by the newtype/quantity/units-of-measure/value-object cluster; ring-buffer-backed queue by ring-buffer; ISR-with-deferred-work by deferred-interrupt-processing; double-buffered DMA by direct-memory-access-dma-transfer aka). Charter probes judged: audio/DSP — no new element (mechanisms already present, biquad rejected as zoo); compilers beyond parsing — rejected (SSA/regalloc zoo), except lr-parser which is parsing-axis proper; scientific computing — parallel-reduction in, stencil in (borderline), halo exchange rejected; CLI subcommand dispatch — rejected; build/config — already covered under code-structure. Naming sources live-verified this session: xunitpatterns.com Four Phase Test, Venti FAST'02, Provos et al. USENIX Sec'03, McCool et al. Structured Parallel Programming; Knuth TAOCP v2, Dragon Book, Lamport CACM 1978 are textbook-canonical. None of the naming sources are existing corpus works (checked work_ids.tsv), so all named_in are free-text for Phase 2 to ingest. Post-merge counts if all 9 accepted: 691 elements; numeric-precision 8->10, parsing-text 18->19, testing-constructs 8->9. Recommendation: freeze the catalog at ~691 and proceed to Phase 2.
